tests.weakness: OpenAPI spec, a leftover Werkzeug route dump, an api-catalog metafile, JS comments and GraphQL introspection together enumerate far more endpoints than the UI uses, including an unauthenticated deprecated legacy endpoint and an undocumented v2 that still work.

tests.surface: GET+PUT /v1/orders/{id}, POST /v1/orders/update (id in body), GET /api/users/{id}/documents, GET+PUT /api/documents/{uuid}
tests.weakness: No ownership checks: user A reads and modifies user B's order via the path id and via an order_id supplied in the JSON body; document UUIDs leaked by the listing endpoint grant read/write access to another user's documents.

Responses return full model objects (password hashes, API tokens, SSNs, internal notes, other users' PII); app.js filters to username+email purely client-side. The undocumented v2 serializer embeds the complete owner record.

The admin guard matches a path prefix plus write methods instead of the caller's role: GET /api/admin/users passes for any user, DELETE order has no role check, and role management outside /api/admin/ lets a normal user promote themselves to admin.

Receiver computes but ignores the provider HMAC, has no event_id/timestamp dedup (replays credit again), trusts the claimed account_id and amount, and fetches an attacker-supplied callback_url server-side, exposing an internal-only metadata service (SSRF).

Server reflection enumerates services/methods and returns the .proto; the channel is plaintext with no auth; regular RPCs require an x-api-token but AdminDumpUsers/AdminSetStock enforce nothing, so anyone dumps password hashes and writes stock.

tests.surface: POST /graphql (introspection, deep nesting, aliased login batch, updateOrderStatus, setUserRole)
tests.weakness: Introspection on, no depth/complexity/alias limits, nested owner fields expose other users' hashes and tokens, aliased login mutations bypass the REST brute-force lockout, and mutations skip object-level and function-level authorization.

Two real clang-built modules (one disguised as .bin, lazy-loaded) retain the name section, DWARF debug info and a producers section identifying the toolchain; exports leak internal function names; data segments embed a live API key, an internal metadata URL and a build flag; the original C source is served alongside.
